response.sql:
WITH sex_groups AS (
  SELECT 
    p.SEX,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    record_count,
    AVG(record_count) OVER () AS avg_count
  FROM sex_groups
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    record_count,
    avg_count,
    SUM(record_count) OVER () AS total_above_avg
  FROM group_stats
  WHERE record_count > avg_count
)
SELECT 
  SEX,
  record_count,
  record_count / total_above_avg AS fraction_of_total,
  record_count - avg_count AS above_average
FROM above_average

assumptions.assumption: "The total over all these groups" refers to the sum of test records for the above-average groups only (those being displayed), not the grand total of all groups.

alternatives.interpretation: "The total over all these groups" refers to the grand total of all laboratory tests across all sex groups (both above-average and below-average), and the fraction should represent each above-average group's share of this global total.
